blockingIssues.title: Reflow still caps each nested placement at 200 expansions and can return a partially applied plan with budgetExhausted: false
blockingIssues.description: packages/reservations/src/engine/assign.ts:1079 passes `maxExpansions: Math.min(MAX_REPAIR_EXPANSIONS /* 200 */, remainingBudget)` into the nested `assignTables` call of `reflowDay`, even though the reflow call itself now has the required 5,000-expansion budget (assign.ts:942-945). When that 200 sub-budget is exhausted while `totalExpansions < maxExpansions`, assign.ts:1137-1148 pushes the booking into `unresolvable` and continues instead of taking the day-budget no-fit reset (assign.ts:1151-1184), so a reflow call can return moves for some bookings plus `unresolvable` for the failed one with `status: 'no_fit'` and `budgetExhausted: false`. architecture.md:1196-1197 requires 'Exhausting a budget returns "no fit" (never a partial plan)', and the normative research gives booking placement the book budget (research/reservation-engineering.md:204-206, 274-276) bounded by the caller's reflow budget. Reachable in the contract's own 120-table/80-combination fixture (one repair attempt iterates roughly 150 occupied candidates in its 1-step loop), and scale.test.ts:86-100 asserts only `expansions <= 5,000` / `budgetExhausted === false`, never `unresolvable.length === 0`, so the partial path has no regression coverage. Validator independently confirmed the code path. Downstream risk: the host-stand milestone builds reflow and auto-move notices on this contract.
blockingIssues.suggestedFix: Pass `Math.min(MAX_BOOK_EXPANSIONS, remainingBudget)` into the nested placement (or treat any nested budget exhaustion as the reflow-level no-fit reset), assert a successful reflow has an empty `unresolvable` in the scale test, and delete the now-competing MAX_DAY_EXPANSIONS/MAX_REPAIR_EXPANSIONS vocabulary.

blockingIssues.title: Property suite does not verify the required invariant semantics (search/book agreement, monotonic release, atomic modify, overbook isolation) while claiming I1-I8
blockingIssues.description: The operation-sequence harness exists (packages/reservations/src/testing/arbitraries.ts:520-954 runs search/hold/book/modify/cancel/seat/finish/no_show/block/settings/clock and calls verifyDayInvariants after every step at :935-947; engine.property.test.ts:128-147), but the invariant set is incomplete: there is no search-then-hold agreement check (engine.property.test.ts:115-117 only asserts returned slots have tableIds), no monotonic-release check (nothing compares availability before/after cancel/seat/finish), no atomic-modify check (arbitraries.ts:722-766 applies engine results only on success, so a partial mutation cannot surface), and no staff-overbook isolation check. Instead, the oracle attaches I6/I7/I8 labels to pacing caps (oracle.ts:229-261), channel/mode eligibility (oracle.ts:76-177) and interval/service-window checks (oracle.ts:78-81, 179-199) - a mapping that matches neither architecture.md:234-239 (I6 atomic modify, I7 search/book agreement, I8 monotonic release) nor skills/domain-worker SKILL.md step 3 (I6 search-hold, I7 monotonic release, I8 failed modify). VAL-FND-009 requires 'invariants I1 through I8 after every step', and mission.md's invariants list includes exactly those semantics. The handoff claims 'check all invariants I1 through I8' with followedProcedure=true and an empty deviations list, which overstates the delivery. Validator independently confirmed by reading oracle.ts, arbitraries.ts:556-954 and engine.property.test.ts.
blockingIssues.suggestedFix: Add the missing per-step checks (hold a searched slot against identical state/clock; compare availability before/after cancel/finish/shrink; assert a failed modify leaves the reservation and its occupancies unchanged; exercise overbook isolation), relabel the oracle to one canonical invariant list, and require the handoff to map each named invariant to the assertion that proves it.

blockingIssues.title: KSA local tenant DB still carries the pre-fix triggers, so the fix's own "US/KSA tenant DBs are in sync" outcome is only 2/3 met (machine state, not code)
blockingIssues.description: Verified by the validator with a read-only sqlite3 SELECT on sqlite_master: packages/database/db/ksa/tenant_ru0dm42cud9scs4g2duep21c.db (the DB services.yaml starts for tenant-api-ksa via TENANT_DB_DIR=packages/database/db/ksa) still defines rsv_occupancy_no_overlap_insert/_update as `RAISE(ABORT, 'table_overlap')` with an EXISTS filter of only `o.active = 1` (no `o.overbook = 0`), and rsv_holds_single_conversion as `WHEN OLD.status = 'converted' AND NEW.status = 'converted'`; the two US-dir DBs (packages/database/db/tenant_*.db) carry the corrected SQL. The DB cannot self-heal: __drizzle_migrations already records 0016, both seed commands are no-ops for an applied migration, and mission rules forbid deleting tenant DB files. Concrete failure path on the local KSA data plane: a normal occupancy (active=1, overbook=0) overlapping an existing staff overbook row still aborts with the retired 'table_overlap' string (which mapSqliteConstraintError no longer maps, so not a 409), and the tightened converted-hold rule does not apply. Later milestones test KSA flows on this node. No validation-contract tool reads this artifact (VAL-FND-011/012 build a fresh temp DB), so the remedy is a data-only trigger refresh rather than a product-code change.
blockingIssues.suggestedFix: DROP/CREATE the affected triggers in packages/database/db/ksa/tenant_ru0dm42cud9scs4g2duep21c.db using the 0016 SQL, then verify sqlite_master in both TENANT_DB_DIR roots; consider adding one reusable refresh command/helper so future in-place migration corrections have an approved tool.

nonBlockingObservations.description: time.ts:99-104 overload soundness hole: `localToInstant(date, min, tz, opts?: LocalToInstantOptions)` claims a non-null result for a widened options variable while the implementation can return null when opts.gap === 'skip' (time.ts:156-158). Latent today (only literal options are passed).

Legacy budget constants MAX_REPAIR_EXPANSIONS (200) and MAX_DAY_EXPANSIONS (2,000) are still exported (assign.ts:24,26); MAX_DAY_EXPANSIONS is unused in src and MAX_REPAIR_EXPANSIONS survives only as the reflow sub-budget. Two names for the same numbers is what caused the original mis-mapping; fold into the blocking fix.

validateConfig reports leading/trailing 1..party_max bucket-coverage gaps with severity 'warning' (validate.ts:526-537, 574-586), so `valid` stays true. VAL-FND-004 only requires detection, so this is a judgement note, not a defect.

On the day-budget reset path, `unresolvable`/`unassignedIds` are set to every soft booking id (assign.ts:1171-1179) even though those bookings keep their original tables; callers must not read it as 'occupancy released'. Consider a distinct field for the host-stand milestone.

Docs written by the fix contain factual drift the next round should fold into a docs pass: ADR 048 section 5 / docs/reservations-plan.md:27-38 name non-existent triggers (rsv_holds_no_overlap_*, rsv_events_no_update/_no_delete) and strings ('rsv_reservation_holds overlap', 'rsv_reservation_events is append-only', redaction via `NEW.payload IS NULL`) where 0016 has 9 triggers raising 'append_only' with redaction via `data = '{"redacted":true}'`; docs/permissions.md:212-216 and ADR 048:211-215 state implied-read rules that do not match packages/reservations/src/permissions.ts:59-61 / apps/app/app/utils/organization/tenant-role-permissions.ts:105-111; ADR 048:44 / plan :22 say 24 rsv_* tables where 41 exist; ADR:215 says four role presets where seven are defined; ADR:255-262 overstates the erase-customer route (apps/tenant-api/src/routes/reservations-internal.ts:100-115 scrubs only rsv_guests). VAL-FND-024's bar (8 permissions + 6 flags) is met, so these are not gate failures, but later milestones copy from the ADR.
